tests.name: KeyValueStore mutation hardening enforces the maximum TTL boundary at exactly 2592000 seconds
KeyValueStore mutation hardening treats a key as expired at the exact expiry instant
KeyValueStore mutation hardening allows overwriting an existing key at the key limit but rejects a new key
KeyValueStore mutation hardening reclaims memory when overwriting a larger value with a smaller one
KeyValueStore mutation hardening subtracts replaced bytes when checking the memory limit on overwrite
KeyValueStore mutation hardening mset over existing keys does not count them toward the key limit
KeyValueStore mutation hardening mset rolls back entirely when the batch exceeds the memory limit
KeyValueStore mutation hardening reports ttl -2 for missing, -1 for no-expiry, and a positive value for a live ttl
KeyValueStore mutation hardening persist returns updated:false for a key that has no expiry
KeyValueStore mutation hardening keys returns sorted results capped by the limit
KeyValueStore mutation hardening get and mget return copies so callers cannot mutate stored state
KeyValueStore mutation hardening health reports keyCount, memory, and processed commands
HTTP API mutation hardening rejects a set body without a value field
HTTP API mutation hardening rejects a top-level array body
HTTP API mutation hardening rejects non-integer ttlSeconds
HTTP API mutation hardening validates mget keys is an array of strings
HTTP API mutation hardening validates mset item shape
HTTP API mutation hardening validates the keys limit range
HTTP API mutation hardening rejects an over-long keys prefix
HTTP API mutation hardening maps domain errors to the correct HTTP statuses
HTTP API mutation hardening returns INVALID_COMMAND for unsupported routes
HTTP API mutation hardening exposes delete, ttl, and persist over HTTP
HTTP API mutation hardening round-trips mset and mget over HTTP
KeyValueStore sets, gets, replaces ttl, and persists entries
KeyValueStore hides expired keys and keeps delete idempotent
KeyValueStore msets atomically, mgets in order, and flushes
KeyValueStore validates key, ttl, value size, and duplicate mset keys
KeyValueStore rejects invalid keys on expire() with INVALID_KEY/KEY_TOO_LONG, not KEY_NOT_FOUND
KeyValueStore measures value size in UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units
KeyValueStore health() rate-limits its expired-key sweep but still converges to accurate counts
HTTP API supports set, get, mget, keys, and health envelopes
HTTP API returns deterministic error envelopes
HTTP API rejects invalid keys on POST /expire with 400 INVALID_KEY, not 404
